mentions.name: Wine Bar
mentions.description: An open-source Wine prefix manager that provides a user-friendly way to run Windows apps on Linux, including Apple Silicon Macs running Linux (arm64 via a 4K-page kernel in a micro-VM with FEX-EMU and an x86_64 rootfs) as well as regular x86_64 Linux. It allows installing Windows components with winetricks before installers run, and automatically places installed Windows executables on a "Desktop" in the UI. Available as a Snap (x86_64 and arm64) from the Snap Store.
mentions.problem: The author was unhappy with existing Wine launchers (Lutris, Heroic, Bottles), none of which support Linux on Apple hardware, and wanted more control (e.g., winetricks support) and more user-friendliness (e.g., installed executables appearing automatically in the UI).
mentions.source_excerpt: Since last summer, I am working on a yet another Wine prefix manager, called Wine Bar [1]. My main motivation was to have a user-friendly and opensource tool that can run (some) Windows apps on my Macbook Air M2 running Linux.
